summary: Automated onboarding gateway for cross-pod Slack channels + templated Confluence runbook deployment
description:
Issue summary:
We need a self-service, auditable gateway that provisions a bundled project surface for new cross-pod initiatives: creates a Slack channel (with tiered permission roles), a Confluence runbook space pre-populated from a template, and a Jira service/project skeleton. The gateway should require an approval step (pod lead + security reviewer) and emit audit logs to our central logging pipeline.

Impact:
Currently onboarding is manual: pod leads request a channel, infra manually grants roles, and runbooks are copied ad-hoc. This causes delays (2-5 business days), inconsistent runbook content, missing audit trails, and occasional over-permissive Slack access which has compliance risks for some pods.

Request / Acceptance criteria:
- Implement an automated provisioning gateway accessible from an internal UI/Slack slash command that:
  - Creates a Slack channel with three predefined roles: owners (full), contributors (message/post), observers (read-only via restricted channel).
  - Instantiates a Confluence space from an approved runbook template with placeholders populated (pod name, owners, lifecycle dates).
  - Optionally creates a Jira service project skeleton with default issue types and labels.
  - Includes a two-step approval workflow: pod lead (auto-approve for designated pods) + security reviewer for pods marked as "sensitive".
  - Emits structured audit events to our Log Pipeline (ELK/Kafka) and writes an entry to an internal provisioning audit Confluence page.
- All created artifacts should include a TTL and automatic archival workflow (e.g., 6 months inactive -> auto-archive notification -> archive).
- RBAC rules should be translated into existing IAM groups and mapped to Slack SSO groups; no ad-hoc member invites.
- Provide an operator runbook and rollback steps; unit/integration tests for the automation.

Background / constraints:
- Security requires that any channel with >50 external collaborators or with the label "sensitive" must trigger a security review.
- Slack API rate limits mean we should batch channel creation calls and handle 429 backoffs gracefully.
- Confluence templating must preserve page-level metadata for future programmatic updates.

Proposed technical approach:
- Implement a GitHub Actions-backed provisioning service that validates requests, kicks off an approval workflow (OpsApprovalBot via Slack), and calls a Terraform module for Jira/Confluence provisioning plus a small service (internal-tools/provisioner) that uses the Slack SCIM API for group-sync and channel creation.
- Store templated metadata in a managed S3 bucket and render with safe placeholders.
- Emit events to Kafka topic provisioning-events and wire into existing audit dashboards.

Risks and guardrails:
- Ensure we do not bypass existing enterprise SSO/SCIM flows; all operations must run under a service account with scoped permissions.
- Rollback plan in case of partially provisioned resources (e.g., Slack created but Confluence failed) must remove the Slack channel and submit a cleanup ticket automatically.

Requested timeline:
- Proof-of-concept within 3 weeks, pilot with two pods in 6 weeks, full rollout Q2.

Attachments:
- Example template: Confluence Runbook v2 (linked in related_confluence_pages)
- Slack UX mockups attached in Slack thread #internal-tools-onboarding
comments: 2026-02-11 - Oliver Grant: Thanks Priya. I've reviewed the acceptance criteria. Need to confirm SSO group mapping dataset from Identity team before we can build SCIM sync. Assigning to internal-tools backlog for POC.

2026-02-13 - Jason Liu: Confirmed. Use attribute 'departmentTag' in our Okta profile; I'll open a scoped service account for the automation. See INT-946500 for Okta service account creation.

2026-02-14 - Security (Amira Sol): We'll need an automated checklist run during approval to flag any pod labeled 'regulated' and require an additional legal approval. Also request PII scanning for Confluence templates.
2026-02-15 - Oliver Grant: Noted. I'll add a conditional step in the approval flow. Starting design doc and will circulate for review.
investigation_notes: Checked existing channel provisioning flows: we have ad-hoc scripts in internal-tools that create channels but they don't manage TTL or Confluence templating.
Found prior attempt in INT-623214 to batch-create channels; aborted due to 429 handling issues. Reuse rate-limit logic from infra/batch-worker#132.
Confluence API preserves page metadata but current template store is spread across team spaces; consolidate to a single managed template bucket.
Identified required Terraform modules: jira-project, confluence-space. Need to add idempotent semantics (create-if-not-exists) to prevent duplication on retry.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Implementation summary: Provisioning gateway implemented as GH Action + provisioner service. Slack channel creation uses SCIM group-sync + Conversations.create, with exponential backoff for 429s. Confluence spaces are created from the managed template S3 bucket and populated with runbook placeholders.
Rollout: Piloted with 'data-platform' and 'evals' pods. No permission regressions observed. TTL/archival notifications sent at 5 months inactivity.
Follow-ups: (1) Automate legal approval hook for 'regulated' pods (INT-951002). (2) Add automated PII scan for new runbook pages (security ticket raised).
